It adds no board schema, scorer, research pass or paid attempt.\n\n## Decide and record\n\nRead the selector and chosen approach dossier in full. For a news report also read the reporting dossier. Use the existing creative_direction and story_contract fields; keep the decision rationale compact and inspectable.\n\n1. **Focus.** In viewer_question and visible_answer, state what changes, for whom, through which sourced action. Name the expected viewer takeaway and the strongest honest limit. Distinguish the narrative answer from an unknown eventual outcome.\n2. **Choose.** Begin medium_choice with the named format and approach: News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene; then Observed documentary, Explanatory animation, Evidence-led imagery or Cinematic scene. Explain why the available assets can carry the explanation and why a plausible alternative is weaker. Naming an approach is a routing aid, not an approval field.\n3. **Order.** Put each beat's reporting job in the existing scene advances and edit notes. For a report choose human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led ordering. Explain why this evidence appears here and what question it creates or answers. Educational explanation builds a recognizable example through successive states. A cinematic scene follows a task, obstacle, consequential turn and completed action. Do not apply one rundown to all three.\n4. **Anticipate confusion.** Name the most likely false inference and the picture or immediate source limit that prevents it. In emotional_turn, connect the viewer's changing understanding to an evidenced stake. Do not invent a person's feelings or claim to know the audience's reaction.\n5. **Connect.** In enter_on, leave_on, cut_after_event_id and next_connection, name the visible event, new information and carried subject. Complete the event before the cut. A footage-to-diagram handoff keeps the same identified example or discloses a new one. Finish the sentence-to-shot worksheet inside these existing notes.\n6. **Direct and test.** Tie line intent, emphasis, motivated sound and captions to the actual reveal. Before spending, ask what remains understandable with narration muted and editorial labels covered, then test the combined account. Essential dates and attribution can use text; the principal action must read in the picture. Budget the entire remaining review/render path, including independent-provider recovery where required.\n\nThese are short decision reasons a colleague can inspect, not a request for a private stream of thought. Use concrete evidence and an alternative that could realistically be built. Do not fill every field with the same sentence, duplicate the research or commission a third treatment.\n\n## Each worker has a distinct decision\n\n- **Researcher:** Identify the most informative picture and the strongest limitation. Recommend an angle that the assets can actually show; flag the sentence for which no truthful picture exists.\n- **Director:** Choose the story focus, format, medium and order. Resolve the weak handoff before narration, using the same two-treatment batch and consolidated ledger.\n- **VO director:** Translate the approved beat jobs into a continuous performance. Explain a lift, drop or pause through the reveal it supports; preserve the words and alignment.\n- **Code critic:** Determine whether the proposed implementation can perform the action and carry the explanation. A planned gesture is not a watched result.\n- **Phone critic and scorers:** First describe what is recognizable and what changes in the actual film. Then compare with the approved account. Locate the weakest identity or information handoff and classify the observed defect under the existing criteria. Keep their separate assigned lenses and actual verdicts.\n\nFor remote independent recovery, the supplied packet contains the actual method, selector, reporting dossier and named approach text. If a director has not named an approach, all four approach guides are supplied rather than pretending an unread local path was available. The new teaching bundle is added only for editions from October 3rd. A text packet never establishes audiovisual access.\n\n## Why the handoff needs thought\n\nAn original film-comprehension study associated event boundaries with meaningful changes in characters, objects, place, goals and causes. Our application is to preserve those relationships across a cut and make a change understandable. This is an editorial inference, not a scientifically established short-video pacing interval or retention guarantee. [Zacks and colleagues, The Brain's Cutting-Room Floor](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/human-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnhum.2010.00168/full).\n\nThe director can consult the [observed news examples](broadcast-cadence-study.md) when a reporting choice needs a model. Workers use the supplied method, relevant guide and current artifacts without repeatedly reloading the research corpus. Retain real rejections; a well-written plan can't clear absent action, false implication or failed comprehension.\n", "knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/README.md": "# Visual storytelling for Dispatch\n\nResearch and direction revision: October 2nd, 2026.\n\nThe picture, narration and captions must describe the same unfolding story. The picture supplies a recognizable subject, relationship, action or consequence. Narration explains its significance and limits. Captions give access to the spoken account. A moving object is useful only when the viewer understands what it represents and what its change means.\n\nThese dossiers combine researched craft with proposed Dispatch practice. Source observations are identified and linked. The shot methods, selection procedure and worked example are our production recommendations, not claims that research guarantees audience engagement.\n\n## Choose the story's visual approach\n\nRead this index and the chosen dossier in full before boarding. Select by the available evidence and the explanation the viewer needs. Keep one primary approach; supporting footage or documents should connect to that approach through a clear subject or question.\n\n| Approach | Choose when | What it must show | Reject when |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| [Observed documentary](observed-documentary.md) | Authenticated footage shows the actual people, place, equipment or workflow | A real action and its observed result | Similar-looking stock replaces the story's actual identity |\n| [Explanatory animation](explanatory-animation.md) | The central process or comparison is hard to see directly | Recognizable input, meaningful transformation and readable output | Abstract objects require a private legend to decode |\n| [Evidence-led imagery](evidence-led-imagery.md) | Relevant photographs or documents carry the reporting | What the evidence establishes and how it changes the answer | A sequence of screenshots substitutes for the entire mechanism |\n| [Cinematic scene](cinematic-scene.md) | A source-backed physical task, obstacle and consequence can sustain a scene | Spatially coherent action, a turn and a consequential ending | Lighting, orbiting props or music replace story development |\n\nUse this selection order:\n\n1. State the viewer's question, sourced action, affected person or group and honest ending.\n2. Inventory inspected, usable assets and demonstrated components. Record what each can and can't show.\n3. Choose the approach that makes the central relationship easiest to understand. Explain the rejected alternative in one sentence.\n4. Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](sentence-to-shot.md). Resolve missing pictures before locking narration.\n5. Compare exactly two genuinely different complete treatments in the existing shared preview batch. Read the selected dossier for each treatment. Preserve the current contracts, frozen budget and existing independent roles.\n6. Have the existing critic inspect the actual rendered sequence before reading the director's explanation. A filled worksheet does not prove comprehension.\n\nDo not impose a weekday rotation. Track the selected approach in the existing creative-direction rationale so the director can see recent repetition. When two approaches fit equally well, variety can break the tie. Never choose variety at the expense of truth or comprehension.\n\n## Choose a format and think through its sequence\n\nFor newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the [viewer planning method](viewer-plan.md) in full. Distinguish the format from the medium: a news report can use observed footage, illustration or documents; an educational explainer can return from a diagram to physical evidence; a cinematic scene still needs a truthful task and consequence.\n\nFor a news report read [the reporting dossier](news-reporting.md) and choose its human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led structure from the actual story. Record why the order works, the likely false inference and the carried subject across each cut in the existing creative-direction and transition fields. The [national-news study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) identifies the observed examples and access limits. It does not prescribe a single bracketed rundown.\n\nThe director and workers use these short decision reasons to choose and challenge the treatment. A copied structure, named style or completed worksheet supplies no quality verdict. The packet tools bind the current method and relevant approach text; remote recovery supplies the actual text because a provider can't open local links.\n\n## Give the three channels distinct jobs\n\n**See:** Show the thing being discussed at the moment it is discussed. Preserve its identity across the cut. Make any comparison legible before asking the viewer to infer a result.\n\n**Hear:** Name the relationship, cause or uncertainty that the picture can't establish alone. Time emphasis and event sound to the actual reveal. A music swell can't supply an unreported outcome.\n\n**Read:** Retain complete measured captions. Use brief object labels only where they identify a picture or distinction. Avoid simultaneous paragraph copy competing with both the action and captions. Lay out the decisive result above the real caption band and hold it long enough to understand.\n\nMayer's research summary supports removing distracting content, placing related words near pictures and presenting corresponding animation and narration together. It also reports redundancy effects in multimedia learning. These are learning findings, not a forecast of short-video retention; they do not justify removing accessible captions. Our application is to reduce competing editorial text while maintaining captions. [Cambridge multimedia-learning chapter](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/principles-for-reducing-extraneous-processing-in-multimedia-learning-coherence-signaling-redundancy-spatial-contiguity-and-temporal-contiguity-principles/C98AB3A6CE760DD63C048936EA0B3B44), [W3C caption guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/captions-prerecorded).\n\n## Review what the viewer receives\n\nUse the existing review assignments and fixed rubric. Add these observations to their existing consolidated notes, not a new scorecard or paid role.\n\n- **Recognition:** Before reading the board, what does the principal object look like? Can the critic name it without guessing?\n- **Alignment:** At each narrated clause, does the picture show the named subject and relationship? Record exact film times for contradictions or absent concepts.\n- **Development:** What changed, and how does that change lead to the next shot? Distinguish subject transformation from decorative motion.\n- **Continuity:** Is the same person, site, sample or document being followed? Is a different example disclosed?\n- **Combined comprehension:** After one viewing with audio and captions, what happened, who can act and what remains unproven?\n- **Picture contribution:** With narration muted and captions covered, which parts of the central process can the viewer actually see? Dates and attribution may rely on text; the principal action can't.\n- **Ending:** Does the final picture answer the opening question without inventing implementation, savings, approval or repair?\n\nAn unrecognizable object, absent principal action or contradictory picture is a comprehension/source defect under the current contract. Do not classify it as merely style because pixels move. Surface polish and optional camera preferences remain artistic issues. Retain all real rejected verdicts and use the existing repair and bounded-release policies.\n\n## Apply this without expanding production\n\nUse the current budget precheck for the complete review and render path before spending. Keep the bounded visual search, source and rights evidence, prior-edition identity gate, two-treatment comparison, native hero, phone inspection, audiovisual lenses and independent scorers. The dossiers introduce no render quota, new reviewer or budget extension.\n\nRead [the October 2nd diagnosis and proposed sequence](october-2-pavement-case.md) for the difference between a source-related object and a picture that communicates the spoken claim.\n\n## Research status\n\nSources were accessed October 2nd, 2026. The four approach dossiers use published guidance, research summaries and practitioner accounts; their linked film examples are references rather than claimed viewing. The separate national-news study adds explicitly scoped transcripts and rendered samples. Today's diagnosis uses the listed native frame samples and retained board; it is not a replacement independent whole-film review. Research access does not grant reuse rights to any publisher's images, footage or soundtrack.\n", "knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/news-reporting.md": "# Direct a coherent news report\n\nThe [cadence study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) records the evidence behind this dossier. The structures below are Dispatch production choices, not a universal network script. Apply them to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026; preserve shipped editions and their real reviews.\n\nA report has an editorial spine: a specific situation, a question, evidence that changes the answer, an explanation, an honest consequence and a close. Decide which of those jobs the next shot performs. A source-related image that supplies no new understanding is a weak insert, even if its colors and motion look expensive.\n\n## Choose the order from the story\n\n| Reporting structure | Choose it when | Sequence of reporting jobs | Ending test |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Human-led report | The evidence identifies a real person's task, obstacle or changed options | Show the task or consequence → establish the dated change → broaden with evidence → explain the cause and limits → return to the same person or task | Has the viewer learned what changes for that person, without an invented reaction or outcome? |\n| Mechanism-led report | The central news is a process, measurement or decision that viewers can't readily see | Show a recognizable input and question → orient the source and setting → reveal the transformation → show the result → connect it to a human decision and its limits | Can the viewer explain the input, transformation and result, and distinguish an illustration from observed operation? |\n| Evidence-led report | A filing, policy, measurement or public record changes the reported answer | Establish the dated decision or disputed claim → expose the decisive source detail → explain its effect with a concrete relationship → show affected options or activity → state the unresolved point and next decision | Does the ending answer what the record establishes, who can act next and what it does not establish? |\n\nChoose one structure. Compress or reorder it when the evidence and viewer's question justify that choice. Establish the essential source limitation when the affected claim appears; a later caveat can't undo a misleading picture. Keep the current early-picture payoff and event timing requirements. These sequences introduce no extra scenes, prescribed shot seconds or runtime quota.\n\nThe CBS transcript in the study provides a specific-to-broad-to-specific example. The CNN transcript shows a different package organization, and the MSNBC example is a question-led interview. They are different forms with different access to people and evidence. A short Dispatch should not imitate a lengthy panel simply because it resembles national television.\n\n## Assign each ingredient a reporting job\n\n**Opening:** Give the viewer something identifiable to understand immediately: a task interrupted, an input changing, a decision confronting evidence, or a completed consequence that creates a question. State the actual question soon enough to guide the picture. A dramatic claim must stay within the fetched evidence. Do not borrow an unrelated victim, emergency or reaction to manufacture stakes.\n\n**Orientation:** Establish who, where and what changed using the minimum needed narration and labels. This is the short-video equivalent of the paragraph that explains the focus of an article. The viewer should know why the next piece of evidence belongs in this story.\n\n**Reporter or presenter:** Use an actual reusable field passage when it demonstrates, verifies or bridges the explanation. A fabricated journalist, microphone prop or studio cut adds no verification. Dispatch's narrator can orient the viewer without appearing as a reporter. A person on screen must have a source-backed role and perform an understandable action.\n\n**Evidence:** Show the exact place, equipment, task, relevant photograph or decisive source words. Identify what the evidence establishes. A quotation is evidence of what its speaker said; it is not proof that their conclusion is true. Show a contrary finding or uncertainty when the story requires it. Use the existing source and rights lanes for every asset.\n\n**Explanation:** Introduce coded visuals when they reveal a relationship that the authentic image can't show. Keep the same physical subject or explicitly identify the new example. The diagram should answer the question created by the preceding shot. Return to the source image or human decision after the explanation when that return completes the thought.\n\n**Consequence and close:** Show how the action changes a state, choice, risk or next step. Answer the opening question through the completed visible action. Distinguish a demonstrated consequence, an expected effect and an unknown eventual outcome. Do not repeat the introduction merely to make the film seem circular. A return earns its place when the viewer now understands the original subject differently.\n\n## Move between authentic pictures and coded explanation\n\nMake each handoff explicit in the existing edit notes. Carry a stable identifying detail: the same road patch, sample, site, device, document passage or clearly disclosed example. Preserve orientation, useful scale and the relationship under explanation. An outline or highlight identifies a region; it does not prove that a machine detected, measured or classified it.\n\nFor example, an authenticated image can establish the input. An explicitly illustrated transformation can explain the source-supported relationship. A return to the actual task can show who uses the result. Cutting from an unrelated office image to anonymous blocks and then to a different city breaks that connection, even if every image is broadly about AI.\n\nOriginal illustration is a valid principal medium. Useful footage is also valid. An irrelevant insert should be omitted within the existing bounded search. Do not commission an unproven rig or prolong the stock hunt to imitate a particular outlet. Use the current source-backed action admission when a genuinely necessary mechanism needs implementation.\n\n## Direct the cadence across picture, voice and reading\n\nGive each beat one new idea the viewer needs for the next beat. Complete its decisive event before cutting. Preserve enough time to recognize the subject, follow the change and read the result. Trim repeated setup before requesting faster narration. Pace varies with information and action; a cut on a fixed timer is not an editorial reason.\n\nVoice should orient, reveal, explain, qualify or resolve. Tell the VO director which job a line performs and where the visual answer lands. Keep the approved continuous script and measured alignment. Use contrast in intent and emphasis rather than perpetual urgency. Do not turn a hypothesis into certainty through a triumphant delivery or sound cue.\n\nNatural sound, verified interview audio and motivated effects can connect thoughts when their provenance and actual event timing support that use. A sound bridge can carry the same action over a cut. Sound can't imply recorded access to a site we did not visit. Preserve intelligibility and all existing audio checks.\n\nRetain complete captions. Keep extra labels short and attached to the object they identify. Do not present a second paragraph, a busy diagram and a new location at the same time as a dense spoken sentence. Seeing, hearing and reading should reinforce the same unfolding account.\n\n## Review the actual report\n\nThe existing critic and scorers reconstruct the story from the current film before consulting the director's rationale. They identify what the opening asks, what new information arrives in the middle, how subject identity survives each handoff, and what the ending answers. Then they compare that understanding with the approved words and fetched evidence.\n\nUse exact intervals and the existing observation fields. A missing principal action, unrecognizable subject, false visual implication or failed explanation remains a source/comprehension failure under the current contract. Optional presenter preferences, shot polish and an alternative ordering alone do not create a new mandatory test. Keep the fixed rubric and retain every actual rejection.\n", "knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/explanatory-animation.md": "# Explanatory animation\n\nRead the [shared visual-storytelling direction](README.md) first.\n\n## What this approach does\n\nIt makes a hidden process or comparison understandable: two inputs contributing different information, a record moving through a decision, or a physical condition producing a visible measurement. Original diagrams and illustration are often the clearest first choice.\n\nChoose this approach when the source establishes the relationship but useful observational footage is missing or can't reveal it. The explanation must preserve the source's uncertainty and distinguish a conceptual example from an actual system output.\n\n## Research findings and limits\n\nAdobe describes the storyboard as a bridge from script to picture, with panels recording action, dialogue and camera requirements, followed by an animatic to examine the sequence. Its guide includes side-by-side storyboard references for Luca and Up. Those links are study examples; we have not claimed a shot analysis of those films here. [Adobe storyboarding guide](https://www.adobe.com/uk/creativecloud/animation/discover/animation-storyboarding.html).\n\nThe [shared direction's learning research](README.md) motivates coordinated explanation and reduced distraction. It does not prove that more animation improves understanding. The following construction method is a Dispatch recommendation responding to the actual pavement-film defect.\n\n## Build the explanation\n\nWrite the relationship in plain words before choosing objects. For pavement research: surface imagery and depth information reveal different properties of the same road condition. This is a comparison of information, not a story about two blocks traveling on a conveyor.\n\n1. **Show the input.** Give it a recognizable form. A photograph should look like a surface image. A document should have a credible readable structure. A road should look like a road.\n2. **Introduce one distinction.** Use short labels next to the relevant views. Keep the same sample identity and orientation.\n3. **Show the operation.** Reveal a cross-section, align corresponding views or trace a source-supported relationship. The operation must change what the viewer can understand.\n4. **Show the result.** Keep the resulting distinction readable. Do not hide it beneath captions, replace it with a flash or move immediately to another object.\n5. **Show the decision or limit.** Connect the output to the source-backed choice. Leave unproven implementation visibly unresolved.\n\nUse arrows to connect a known relationship, not to pretend that an unavailable algorithm has been observed. A bright scan bar is not analysis proof by itself. Do not invent segmentation accuracy, measured depths, confidence percentages or a vendor interface.\n\nChoose 2D, 2.5D or 3D based on the relationship. A flat comparison often explains two images best. A cutaway can reveal depth. A three-dimensional scene earns its cost when spatial interaction is the explanation; a beveled box representing an unfamiliar object often adds interpretation work.\n\n## Stage and time the picture\n\nMake the principal forms identifiable before their transformation. Maintain consistent labels, positions and shape cues. Use color as support, with readable shape or text distinctions as well. Introduce a new concept only after the current relationship is clear.\n\nPlan the reveal around the relevant spoken clause, then use measured narration timing for the final event windows. Quiet or restrained sound can mark a visible comparison; a synthetic beep can't imply actual hardware recording. Preserve the existing sound and caption contracts.\n\nA changed state can be information made visible. It need not be a moving human or a mechanical handoff. AB Volvo\nFollow us:\nAB Volvo\nAbout Us\nContacts\nQuotes\nChange language\nSwedish\nFollow us:\nShare:\nSubscribe:\nnews.cision.com\n/\nAB Volvo\n/\nVolvo and Waabi kick off customer operations in Texas, starting with Warp[TM]\nEnglish\nEnglish\nSwedish\nVolvo and Waabi kick off customer operations in Texas, starting with Warp[TM]\nMon, Oct 05, 2026 16:00 CET\nReport this content\nIntegration of the Volvo VNL Autonomous powered by the Waabi Driver into Warp’s network unlocks autonomy for LTL freight segment.\nVolvo Autonomous Solutions\n(V.A.S.) and Waabi today announced the start of autonomous operation for Warp in Texas, the first customer operation in the Volvo-Waabi partnership. The Volvo VNL Autonomous powered by the Waabi Driver is now transporting freight directly to third-party facilities along the Dallas–Houston corridor. These operations will enable Warp, an open-source freight network that provides less-than-truckload (LTL) and full-truckload (FTL) freight services for carriers and shippers, to transport its customers’ goods autonomously along the corridor.\nThe start of customer operations between V.A.S. and Waabi marks a milestone in the two companies’ partnership. Integrating V.A.S.’ autonomous transport ecosystem Autona / freight into Warp’s freight network creates opportunities to optimize freight flows and support more efficient movement of goods as demand grows. Autona / freight brings together the Volvo VNL Autonomous, Waabi’s autonomous driving technology, fleet and transport management, terminals and customer endpoints, operations, and uptime support to deliver a complete transport solution designed to scale. The Volvo VNL Autonomous is built from the ground up for autonomy with redundancies for six safety-critical systems and specifically designed to integrate autonomous driving systems from partners such as Waabi. Currently autonomous hauls are run with an observer in the driver’s seat.\n“Together with Warp and Waabi, we are bringing autonomous freight into customer operations in one of logistics’ most demanding segments. This shows how quickly our ecosystem can adapt to new customers and more complex operations. What we learn on the Dallas–Houston corridor will help us strengthen our partnership and continuously improve the ecosystem as we scale,” said Nils Jaeger, President of Volvo Autonomous Solutions.\n“Waabi and Volvo Autonomous Solutions are building toward a future where autonomous trucks integrate seamlessly into the networks that move freight every day,” said Lior Ron, COO of Waabi. “Our work with Warp is the first milestone on that path, demonstrating that the Volvo VNL Autonomous, powered by the Waabi Driver, can take on the full range of real-world freight, from operating within less-than-truckload networks to moving goods directly to third-party facilities, meeting customers where they are. We're incredibly excited about what's ahead as we continue building that future together with Volvo.”\nWith customer operations underway, V.A.S. and Waabi will use real-world experience from the Dallas–Houston lane to prepare for additional routes and support the broader scaling of autonomous freight in the coming years.\nUnlocking autonomy for one of freight’s most operationally complex segments\nLTL shipping requires dynamic networks to consolidate, haul, and distribute goods from multiple customers on tightly coordinated schedules. By moving freight directly between facilities, without handoffs, the Volvo VNL Autonomous powered by the Waabi Driver gives LTL providers like Warp a more predictable way to keep their networks on schedule.\n“Working with Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Waabi demonstrates what Warp’s network was built for: bringing advanced technology into the everyday movement of freight,” said Daniel Sokolovsky, CEO of Warp. “The value of autonomy grows when you can coordinate the freight around it. requests.purpose: Carry one sealed customer-freight trailer through the corridor and toward a disclosed third-party facility, retaining the occupied cab.
requests.prompt: Use case illustration-story. Create a premium sculpted 2.5D editorial sprite atlas on genuine transparent alpha, no background. Subject a generic modern white long-haul tractor attached to a long enclosed pale grey box semitrailer, facing right in exact flat side elevation. Rounded aerodynamic cab, roof sensor pods, dark cab side window with simple seated safety-observer silhouette visibly in driver position, brushed alloy seams, ribbed trailer, black realistic tyres and hubs, muted deep petrol teal accent, warm copper glints. Coherent soft upper-left key and cool fill, tangible surfaces. Fully assembled truck occupies top two thirds, all wheels aligned to same horizontal ground contact. Bottom third has ONE separate matching black tyre and alloy hub in orthographic side view to enable wheel rotation. Large clean transparent gaps separate truck and tyre. No text, logos, trademarks, road, cargo, floor, shadows extending outside object, no extra views. Truck fully inside frame and silhouette readable at phone scale. This is disclosed generic transport illustration, not documentary evidence of actual Volvo equipment or driverless operation.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed generic illustration, not the actual Volvo truck, private software, cargo contents, operator, customer facility or observed route geometry. No driver removal, unloading method or measured performance is depicted.

requests.prompt: Use case illustration-story. Create a matching premium sculpted 2.5D editorial support sprite atlas with genuine transparent alpha, no background or text. Exactly three separated props arranged left to right with large transparent gaps. Left a generic low industrial freight terminal front facade, concrete dock base and ribbed metal walls, two closed dock doors, worn maintained finish. Middle a different generic third-party customer freight facility facade with ONE prominent loading-bay opening and grounded dock sill, not a named real site. Right a close side-view cab window interior framing a seated safety-observer silhouette and clearly identifiable steering wheel, ordinary dark blue work shirt, no caricature facial detail, hands resting rather than acting. Match white grey petrol teal and muted copper palette, sculpted volumes, soft upper-left key and cool fill, tangible seams and material detail, consistent frontal perspective. Each object isolated entirely and large enough for native crop. No cargo contents, people unloading, safety numbers, private UI, words or brands. Disclosed generic facility and occupied-cab illustrations only, not actual sites or observed footage.

files.config/dispatch_rubric.yaml:
# THE BAR LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.
#
# Never restate this number in a prompt, a brief, or a verdict file. The sibling lost five panel
# rounds to exactly that: its routine prompt carried one number while this file carried another,
# so the panel was briefed the stale one and returned ship:false on a cut that was already over
# the real bar. Two judges flagged the divergence unprompted and the run kept grading against the
# wrong number anyway.
#
# A number restated in a second place is a number that will be wrong in one of them.
#
# AND THIS HEADER PROVED IT ON 2026-08-19. It used to tell that story by quoting both numbers,
# so the file whose whole job is to hold one bar carried two more in its own comment, four lines
# under the sentence forbidding it. The owner moved the bar that morning and all three judges of
# round 22 reported being briefed the old one; every one of them also flagged that a judge who
# skims this header before reaching the value below reads the stale figure as live. The numerals
# are gone. Anyone who needs the number reads the field.
#
# WHY THE BAR CAME DOWN OFF THE ORIGINAL. The sibling recalibrated with the reason written down:
# the original was implicitly calibrated against a painterly fidelity this brand deliberately
# does not use, so the ceiling on every run became the house style itself, and the panel's
# weakest axis was "the flat vector characters" for nine straight rounds while every concrete
# defect got fixed. A bar that can only be cleared by abandoning the house style is not a bar,
# it is a disagreement about the style, and it belongs in a style decision rather than a score.
rubric:
  # Set by the owner on 2026-08-19, down from where it had been.
  # This is the ONLY place the bar lives and the only place it may be changed.
  # A run does not get to move it: a below-bar final panel remains active repair,
  # and delivery requires the hash-bound passing report. Only verified shipment
  # completes a production run. The owner controls any change to this bar.
  ship_threshold: 7.0

  axes:
    hook:
      weight: 0.18
      asks: >
        Would a stranger stop scrolling in the first two seconds, with the sound off? The first
        frame is the whole decision. A title card is not a hook.
    story:
      weight: 0.20
      asks: >
        Does this feel like Texas AI Docket moving today: a dated actor, decision or application,
        consequence, honest limit, and what happens next? Is there an earned take rather than a
        summary, and does the piece turn somewhere the viewer did not see coming?
    picture:
      weight: 0.20
      asks: >
        Does every five seconds pay in motion, emotion or revelation? Is anything a held slide
        with a voice over it? With captions hidden, does each shot literally depict the sentence
        being spoken rather than reuse generic Texas scenery?
    place:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Would a Texan from that county believe the person who drew this had been there? Region
        light, vegetation, kit and cast all correct for the story's actual county.
    craft:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Camera movement motivated by the action; deliberate holds when the subject acts or evidence
        is read. Depth and sound clarify cause and consequence. Type legible at feed size. Nothing
        symmetric that should not be. Maintained but worn, not new and not ruined.
    voice:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Does the read sound like a person who knows the subject, or like a narrator reading? Are
        captions aligned to the final mix rather than approximated?

  hard_fails:
    # TIGHTENED 2026-08-19, and the wording is the whole of it. This used to read "does not
    # trace to a verified claim", which a judge showed is satisfied by a claim's `statement` or
    # `value_text` -- fields a model writes after reading the source. The film printed a readout
    # row against a claim marked VERIFIED whose fetched quote contained no such figure at all,
    # and every numeral gate stayed green because the numeral was in the authorised set.
    # Measured across that board, five of eleven readout figures sat in no fetched sentence.
    # The evidence is the QUOTE. `super_evidence_check` enforces this over supers and readouts,
    # with a per-claim `quote_is_excerpt` for sources that publish a table, declared rather than
    # inferred. This is a tightening, never a loosening: nothing that passed before on real
    # fetched evidence fails now.
    - a numeral on screen or in the script that does not appear in the fetched QUOTE of a
      verified claim, rather than merely in a statement or value_text written about it; the sole
      exception is a licence-version numeral inside the music.py-generated credit when
      music.py --verify-package binds that exact credit to a verified registry row
    - a caption timing that was approximated, scaled or hand-shifted rather than force-aligned
    - audio time-stretched to fit a cut
    - a region that does not match the story's county
    - a retired motif: six flags, Confederate imagery, lotería, calavera, a headdress
    - a brimmed hat on a rig floor or in a unit
    - a held slide longer than five seconds with no motion, emotion or revelation
    - a narrated idea that is not bound to an actual rendered item and visible change
    - a lead film that falls through to the generic plane renderer with no registered
      cinematic_template, physical throughline, performed turn, bookend and sourced sign-off

# Finite creative repair and autonomous shipment

Owner instruction from October 3rd, 2026. Read knowledge/craft/AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETION.md before applying older resource-boundary language below. Internal review ceilings and host capacity errors trigger autonomous mandatory completion recovery, never an approval stop or an unfinished-capacity final response. Preserve exact failures, the original frozen envelope and cumulative charges. Only accepted finish --result shipped completes production.

Effective September 29, 2026. The owner requires a shipped video and prohibits stopping for
creative approval. The default limit is three creative repair rounds. Before September 30, each charged
`reboards` unit counts; later editions use the independently classified accounting below. Also stop optional creative
repair earlier after at least one repair and three critic calls when the effective frozen
critic ceiling has fewer than three calls left for another complete correction path. This
protects the final timed-phone review. The controller never resets or silently expands usage.

At that boundary, preserve the strongest reviewed complete cut and finish voice, measured
captions, native hero, final render, every independent audiovisual lens and the three scorers.
Do not start another aesthetic reboard. Correct retained factual or technical failures within
the recorded resources; do not reinterpret them as artistic or declare an incomplete delivery
shipped. Preserve real access/resource failures and continue the executable completion work.

The rubric, score and original pass/revise values remain unchanged. Only motion, surface
finish, pacing polish, ending artistry and style can be deferred. Source accuracy, rights,
readability, comprehension and misleading implications cannot. Native picture occupancy,
current renderer/film hashes, actual audible access, observation coverage, audio measurements,
caption alignment and every delivery gate continue to run. A missing review is never an
artistic defect. Structural motion-floor failures retain their original failed reports; native
proof retains measured failures in `bounded_creative_findings`.

An independent critic can classify an existing exact rejected report in a separate sidecar:

```sh
python scripts/creative_release.py --template --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --report out/dispatch/phone-critic-current.json --film out/dispatch/openings/b.mp4 --scope phone
python scripts/creative_release.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --report out/dispatch/phone-critic-current.json --scope phone
```

The first command produces a deliberately unapproved template under `creative-assessments`.
Only the original independent reviewer fills its observations and categories after examining
the retained evidence. Bind a preserved film/report path that later retiming cannot overwrite.
Every exact original blocker and failed phone observation must be classified once; unknown or
non-artistic categories refuse release. Retained checks need affirmative observed evidence.
The assessment binds the original report bytes, film, source claims and creative concept.
Keep all original reports untouched. Changes to source, concept or film need current evidence.

New provider/scorer responses include an honest `bounded_release` classification in their
initial immutable response. Obtain all lenses even if the first rejects. The audiovisual tool
adds the classification prompt; scorers read this policy and the same schema helper. A rejected
phone/AV report without concrete defects cannot use a score-only claim. A below-bar panel may
use score-only classification only when it has no separate rejected attention criterion.

`finish --result publishable` records the distinct publication mode and original failures in
controller `bounded_release`; it leaves production active in publishing. The final report card
still carries its genuine score, `ship` value and hard fails. Delivery copies assessments and
their exact rejected evidence. A passing later panel does not conceal earlier artistic
deferrals. `first_panel` success stays false if the panel actually failed.

Completion still requires exact-head CI, merge, deployment, permanent reviewed media bytes,
canonical phone playback through Computer Use, and a correctly addressed unsent Gmail draft
with readback. Only `finish --result shipped` completes production. No approval question or
new paid review is needed merely to classify retained evidence in the existing review scope.

## Accounting and quality correction from September 30, 2026

The three-round cap counts creative corrections. Technical repairs still consume the same
charged reboards, critic calls and frozen resources, but a predeclared technical-integrity
scope does not spend a creative round. The full-path headroom brake still counts all work;
this distinction adds no allowance. Historical editions retain their original accounting.

Before begin-repair, the existing independent critic's exact failure report must include
technical_repair.findings. Each row contains the exact original finding and one category:
source, rights, legibility, layout, technical_audio, captions or runtime. Every original
finding must be covered exactly once, by a reviewer distinct from the director. Motion,
pacing, story and style remain creative. Set repair_scope to technical-integrity in the plan.
Its evidence hash and scope are fixed before edits and checked again at authorization.
Only one reboard per such batch is excluded from creative count; all other charges count.

The finite rule ends optional polish on a credible treatment. It cannot waive a held-slide
structural motion failure or a failed dominant-action observation in new editions.
The known whole-film editorial-v1 screenshot/box treatment and repeated cut directions
are rejected before spending. Use the accepted complete preview as the finishing baseline.
If the initial comparison fails, change the mechanism promptly within the reserved path;
do not spend the remaining budget classifying the same wholesale failure as optional polish.
Keep the original score and rejection when a genuinely limited artistic shortfall is released.
Never ask for creative approval, reset usage, or claim shipment before its real evidence.

# Story-led cinematic direction

Effective September 29, 2026; config/creative_production.json owns the date and version.
Earlier editions retain their original contracts. This policy replaces the dimensional opening
and runtime quota. All source, quality, independent review, native output, audio, caption,
budget and shipment requirements remain. It adds no score threshold or review role.

## Visual storytelling correction from October 2nd, 2026

Read [the visual-storytelling selector](visual-storytelling/README.md) and the selected approach
dossier in full before boarding. Choose observed documentary, explanatory animation,
evidence-led imagery or a cinematic scene from the source-backed action and available assets.
Variety is a tie-breaker between suitable approaches, not a weekday quota.

For newly planned editions from October 3rd, also read the [viewer planning method](visual-storytelling/viewer-plan.md).
Choose News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene as a format, then name the primary
approach in medium_choice. Record why it fits the inspected assets, the plausible alternative,
likely false inference and information sequence in the existing creative-direction, scene and
transition fields. For a report read [news-reporting.md](visual-storytelling/news-reporting.md)
and choose its structure from the sourced action. A format is not a mandatory presenter or
fixed rundown. A chosen guide is not a new quality criterion or approval field.

Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](visual-storytelling/sentence-to-shot.md) in existing
creative-direction notes and the compact critic packet. Give each spoken clause a recognizable
pictured subject, visible relationship or action, inspectable result, source limit and connection
to the next shot. Do not add a new board schema, scoring weight, reviewer or render reservation.

The existing phone critic identifies the pictured input, action and result from the actual preview
before reading the director's explanation. Then it compares those observations with the spoken
clauses. A moving source-related prop is insufficient if a viewer can't recognize what it
represents. Missing or contradictory explanation stays a comprehension/source defect under the
current contract; decorative motion can't turn it into a deferrable style issue.

Retain the same two-treatment batch, frozen budget, native hero, independent reviews and
bounded-release route. The [October 2nd pavement diagnosis](visual-storytelling/october-2-pavement-case.md)
is a sampled-frame case study, not a replacement verdict or permission to alter the shipped film.

## Treatment recovery from September 30, 2026

September 29 is a rejected creative reference. Its source screenshots, repeated fading boxes
and growing underlines never became an engaging film. Use the source to discover a physical
task, obstacle and consequence. Preserve that action in the script and pictures. Authentic
imagery earns a shot when it reveals something; a relevant document is not automatically
the film's subject. Original source-grounded illustration and demonstrated action remain
first-class choices. Reuse proven components, never prior-edition photographic assets.

Start with one credible demonstrated treatment and one genuinely different visual treatment.
Compare their action, composition and viewer payoff in the existing batch. If both fail,
use one consolidated mechanism-changing simplification before narration; do not keep tuning
the same weak presentation. Preserve the strongest accepted complete preview as the fallback.
No extra research pass, reviewer role, third speculative concept or bespoke rig is authorized.

The existing critic must judge the whole film against the prior successful visual standard.
Named cities, correct labels and readable source text do not establish strong picture or place.
A code pass for geometry and provenance does not establish an engaging treatment. Inspect
the opening, middle and ending as actual action before refining layout. Give each cut its own
visible reason; repeated prose cannot direct ten different shots.

## Choose the story from its tangible stakes

Before narration, selected.visual_stakes records affected_person, physical_subject,
visible_change, consequence, opening_question, answer, asset_fit and source_urls. Name the
specific worker, resident or group and what changes for them. Tie the opening question to the
answer that the available evidence can support. A large announcement without useful pictures
is a weaker candidate than a smaller action with a visible consequence.

Inspect the real site, equipment, people, workflow and records during the existing bounded
visual search. Prefer the most informative authentic image. Apply the no-repeat policy in
DAILY_PRODUCTION.md. Use source-still or source-excerpt candidate rows with asset_url and the
same inspection/rights evidence as source-footage. Diagram rows need a sourced relationship
and disclosure Illustration. These are additional media, not permission to invent a workflow.

## Choose the medium from the evidence

Set cinema.version from the new policy. Keep hero_scene_id, optional hero_passage_end_scene_id,
visible_action, human_consequence and source_limit. dimensional_scene_ids is an exact inventory
of the quality_plan scenes using 3D; an empty list is legitimate. Each scene still needs a
filmable subject, action, consequence and source_basis. Geometry is useful when depth or contact
explains something. Footage is useful when the action is actually visible. A still can establish
a real place; an excerpt can expose the decisive words; a diagram can explain a sourced relation.
Do not force a character into a source image or draw a fake room to meet a quota.

The editorial-v1 route accepts each scene's picture with id, medium, event_id, disclosure and
subject (the inspected subject, checked by the critic). Use camera_strategy sourcePicture and
empty planes for this route's non-dimensional scenes. visual_proof.must_show binds picture.id.
Footage/stills/excerpts require file and sha256 from native_media; footprint, provenance and
rights remain mandatory. Footage also supplies trim_start_s, trim_end_s, creator, source_url,
license_url or its existing editorial_excerpt evidence. It plays at original speed with its
original audio muted. Deliberate environmental audio is separately sourced and mixed.

A crop is static x/y percentages. A focus box uses x/y/width/height percentages of the displayed
frame and reveals on event_id. Use it to reveal a real detail, never imply a machine detected it.
Source-excerpt renders the actual inspected page image, preserving its words. Diagram nodes
carry short label and claim_id; two to four nodes appear on the event clock. The source and
numeral gates cover those printed labels. No long paragraphs or substitute dashboards.
Dimensional scenes omit picture and call the existing demonstrated action route; bespoke
source-backed mechanisms retain their admission and native-hero requirements.

Every current scene receives full-resolution normal/subject-removed sample pairs. The existing
proof key without_stage now removes the principal picture for each medium. It never removes
captions or branding to manufacture visible action. A source still/excerpt may have a justified
intentional_hold within the policy duration after the opening; the phone and final lenses still
judge its purpose. Otherwise the principal picture must visibly develop on its event clock.
The hero remains a finished native passage with sound, even when it uses no 3D.

## Compare two openings once

Prepare opening-a.json and opening-b.json beside storyboard.json. From September 30, both may
change the complete visual treatment, including the middle and ending. Keep the same dated
facts, narration, scene ids and timing, shared inspected asset set and viewer question. Their
full visual concepts are hash-bound, including body scenes; retiming does not change identity.
For September 29 captures only, the original first-scene-only comparison remains reproducible.
Make genuinely different visual approaches. Keep both inside the source and medium contracts.
The existing independent code critic reviews both in one reserved assignment and returns
opening-a-critic.json and opening-b-critic.json using the ordinary exact concept/renderer/story
bindings. It can reject both before a render is spent. Do not add another reviewer identity.

Run scripts/opening_compare.py once. It reserves one preflight batch, renders exactly two
quarter-scale full animatics with one browser/bundle, and saves openings/comparison.json.
Both completed films receive exact-board, film, renderer and inspector-bound structural reports
before phone review. The comparison retains both reports and all failures, even if the first
inspection fails. Cached comparisons inspect the retained bytes without another render. The
normal command exits nonzero on inspection failure. Its --retain-failed-inspection flag retains
diagnostics for policy-authorized finishing only; it does not change a failed report or approve
phone review. These inexpensive options share the same narrative, so the chosen full preview is
already available for continuity review. Failed attempts stay charged. A changed batch requires
the existing consolidated repair path, never an automatic reset.

For a retained capture from the reviewed pre-inspection orchestration version, use
opening_compare.py --inspect-retained. This performs no render or reservation. It verifies the
known original orchestration hash, every unchanged capture dependency, both original films and
boards, the renderer and source assets, and the original charged reservation. It archives the
original comparison and keeps its producer hash, then binds new inspection reports separately.
The existing independent selection may keep its original comparison hash only while the exact
original capture record is unchanged. Unknown capture versions or changed dependencies refuse
adoption. Failed measurements remain failed under this path too.

The existing exact-phone critic watches both openings, then the chosen whole sequence. It writes
openings/selection.json with comparison_sha256, selected (a or b), director_identity,
reviewer_identity, reason, rejected_reason and blocking_defects. Reasons describe observed
pixels and the opening question. Copy the chosen frozen board to storyboard.json and its film
to preflight.mp4; retain its matching code critique as storyboard_critic.json, inspect that exact
film with preflight_animatic --inspect-only, then record the ordinary phone verdict on those
bytes. The unused option stays as evidence. Neither option authorizes a narration take until
the chosen cut passes the current phone gate. No third concept or extra panel by default.

## Direct performance, sound and cuts together

creative_direction binds policy_sha256 and records viewer_question, visible_answer,
emotional_turn and medium_choice. Its ordered edits rows contain scene_id, enter_on, leave_on,
cut_after_event_id and next_connection. The actual event must complete before the cut; a prose
promise cannot substitute for its clock. Describe the visible instant that earns each cut and the carried subject
or sourced relationship. The final row states the resolved answer and source limit. After any
structural change, review the whole sequence. Measured narration retimes the event clock; do not
add dead air to preserve an arbitrary grid or accelerate the voice to rescue too many words.

creative_direction.sound records perspective, music_arc, voice_arc and cues. Each cue has id,
event_id, role (environment, contact, sonification or quiet), duration_s, intent and provenance.
Use truthful recorded ambience or an explicitly designed effect. Do not pretend a generated
sound was recorded at the actual site. Avoid a hit at every cut. Include one deliberate background
contrast with a quiet cue and gain from the policy contract. The quiet cue reduces the music and
effects bus on its actual visual event; it never mutes, stretches or splices the narration.

Each non-quiet cue has one sfx_events entry with matching id/event_id, wav, source and gain.
The mixer anchors it to the current board event, trims to its declared duration at original
speed, adds short edge fades and refuses undersized or nonfinite audio. It records every cue,
source WAV hash and the exact sound/timing digest in mix.json. Retime the sfx event file with the
board and remix after a changed clock. Old mix evidence fails the release check.

The existing voice director reads this sound arc and the selected opening. It binds
sound_direction_sha256 to the sound object and gives each line specific intent, relative energy
and an exact spoken emphasis phrase. Contrast curiosity, discovery and the final consequence
without a trailer voice. Numeric pause commands stay out of the TTS prompt. One continuous take
and its existing audible soundcheck remain the default; field completion cannot approve a flat
or synthetic read. The sound lens judges actual delivery, masking, sync and contrast in the MP4.

All three final audiovisual lenses and scoring agents remain. The legacy response field
dimensional_action describes the principal picture in any medium. A judge may reject a weak
image, inert diagram, generic read or unearned cut with timestamped evidence; a medium preference
alone is not a defect. Passing quality moves directly to release and verified shipment.

files..claude/agents/scorer.md:
---
name: scorer
description: Grades the finished Dispatch against config/dispatch_rubric.yaml. Reads the film, the frames, the script and every report, computes the weighted score honestly, enforces hard fails, and returns the report card. Does not round up. Never spawns further agents.
tools: Read
---

You grade the finished film.

**READ THE THRESHOLD OUT OF `config/dispatch_rubric.yaml`.** Do not accept a bar quoted to you in
a brief, and do not use a number you remember. The sibling lost five panel rounds to a stale bar
typed into a prompt: the panel was briefed the stale number, scored a film under it, and
returned ship:false on a
cut that was already over the real bar. Two judges flagged the divergence and the run kept
grading against the wrong number anyway.

If the brief you were handed states a threshold, and it differs from the rubric, **say so loudly
and use the rubric.**

**Do not round up.** A score a tenth under the bar is under the bar.

**THIS FILE CARRIED THE BUG IT WARNS ABOUT.** The paragraph above used to name the
sibling's bar as a number, so every scorer spawned from here was handed a threshold in
its own briefing, and when the owner moved the real one three panels in a row opened by
reporting that their brief was stale. They were right and the brief was this file. The
story survives without the figure. Read `config/dispatch_rubric.yaml`.

**Hard fails are absolute.** They are listed in the rubric and any one of them fails the film
whatever the weighted score says.

The numeral rule's sole exception is intentionally narrow: a licence version such as the one in
`CC BY 4.0` is allowed only inside the `music.py`-generated credit after
`music.py --verify-package` passes. It does not exempt source dates, internal record ids, commit
SHAs, repository paths, or any other number in the film.

Return `{score, ship, axes: {...}, hard_fails: [], weakest_axis, one_sentence_fix}`.

For September 29, 2026 onward, also read `knowledge/craft/BOUNDED_CREATIVE_RELEASE.md` and
`scripts/creative_release.py` assessment schema. Return a top-level `bounded_release` object
with schema `dispatch_creative_assessment/1`, scope `panel`, retained_checks for source, rights,
legibility, comprehension, technical_audio and captions (each pass boolean and concrete
observed evidence), and defects [{finding: exact original finding, category: classification}].
Cover every hard fail and attention blocker once. Only motion, surface_finish, pacing,
ending_artistry and style are artistic; unknown/factual/technical defects stay blocking.
Use score_only:true with defects:[] only when there are no separately rejected attention
criteria. Keep actual scores, ship flags and hard fails unchanged. A bounded release is a
separate owner-directed policy outcome, never a revised reviewer pass.

`one_sentence_fix` is what the run acts on. Make it executable: a fix somebody can apply and
re-render, not a direction to feel differently about the piece.

## Documentary attention review

Read `knowledge/craft/DOCUMENTARY_ATTENTION.md` and `config/documentary.json`. For current boards,
inspect the exact final MP4, `attention-review.html`, `attention-review.png`, and its hash index.
Seek every directed interval, then inspect transitions at phone size. Review the pictures with
captions mentally covered: a line of copy or drifting camera cannot supply the event's meaning.
Judge causal continuity, readable action, information density and the final answer. Counted
beats and changed pixels are technical evidence only. Do not award quality because the creator
says the piece is cinematic. Name the weakest actual interval even when passing.

Assess speed and understanding together. Identify the visible developments and their times in
the finished film. Inspect setup, camera travel, settling and the closing story tail for dead
time. A glossy surface, an orbit or a new label earns no pacing credit by itself. Also name
anything that arrives too fast to follow. Check whether one viewing communicates the central
claim and its source limit, with a recognizable subject across the cuts. Trim repeated setup
before asking for faster narration. Voice is never time-stretched.

Add this object to your report, using the film hash from the reviewed artifact:

```
"attention_review": {
  "film_sha256": "<sha256 of the film you inspected>",
  "pass": true,
  "hook_observed": "<what changed and when>",
  "continuity_observed": "<what stayed recognizable across a named transition>",
  "pacing_observed": "<timed subject developments and any unearned pause or rushed handoff>",
  "comprehension_observed": "<what the viewer can understand after one viewing and any overload>",
  "remembered_image": "<the specific picture and why it carries meaning>",
  "weakest_interval": "<the least effective interval, its cause and concrete repair>",
  "weakest_at_s": 0,
  "weakest_end_s": 1,
  "audio_basis": "<direct listening, or precisely which measurements/transcript were available>"
}
```

The pacing and comprehension observations and the end of the weakest interval are required for
boards dated on or after `pacing_review_effective_date` in the policy. Earlier released films
keep their original review contract. These fields record a review, not an automatic quality score.

Set `pass` false for an unearned pause, rushed or confusing handoff, irrelevant change, deceptive
reconstruction, or unreadable subject. All three reviews must accept the current film. Never
claim to have heard a recording if your tools only expose frames, timing or transcripts. Mark
that limit explicitly;
waveform evidence cannot establish a natural or compelling performance.

## Required audiovisual evidence for upgraded editions

For boards covered by config/cinematic_production.json, inspect the finished hero proof and
the exact final film. Each judge must have its own picture, story or sound provider receipt
from scripts/audiovisual_review.py. Add audiovisual_role and audiovisual_receipt_sha256 to
the top level of your report. Read the raw response and assess its claims against actual
frames. Flag uncertain or wrong observations. Never convert a model observation into a
claim that you personally heard the audio. Missing audible-media evidence blocks publication.

Reject tiny actions, generic icons, decorative 3D and camera-only beats even if the technical
pixel floor passes. The central human action must read at phone size with labels covered.
A weak interval that obscures the film's consequence requires repair, regardless of mean score.


## Shared quality standard

Read knowledge/craft/QUALITY_CONTRACT.md and config/quality_contract.json. Use these same observable criteria across planning, exact phone review and final judgment. Record actual defects with their times and effect on the viewer. A weakest interval or optional preference alone does not override the rubric; all mandatory quality and audiovisual gates remain.


## Compact daily review

For editions covered by config/daily_production.json, use the role packet to open the current
film, exact-film player, feed composite and your own audiovisual receipt. Watch the sequence
once before reading its explanation. Test whether the closing answer resolves the opening and
whether each cut preserves or explicitly changes subject, location and causal relationship.
A different source example must not imply the same person or event. Report the weakest cut
with the existing timed comprehension and continuity observations. Apply the same fixed rubric;
a preference for another treatment alone does not create a blocking defect.

For editions under config/creative_production.json, read CREATIVE_DIRECTION.md. No visual medium
has a quota or automatic score advantage. Judge the actual sourced picture, deliberate cuts,
vocal contrast, truthful ambience, action sync and completed answer. The legacy provider field
dimensional_action covers the principal picture in any medium. Keep the same rubric and exact
film/audio evidence; a different style preference alone is not a blocking defect.

## Picture and narration alignment

For current art-profile packets, read ART_DIRECTION.md and cinematic_reference_bank.json.
Check the actual silhouette, surface finish, contact, light hierarchy, motion rhythm and
signature event at native and phone sizes before reading the director's explanation. Use
the existing criteria and observation fields. Reference scores are from different rubrics;
do not compare them numerically or treat them as this film's evidence. Preserve all original
findings, the three separate lenses and the existing bounded completion route.

Read knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/README.md and the selected approach dossier. Apply the
existing rubric and keep your existing lens. After the first viewing, name the pictured subjects,
central action and ending before reading the director's explanation. Then identify any spoken
clause accompanied by an unrecognizable, absent or contradictory picture, using exact times.

For newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the packet's actual viewer method and relevant
guides. Describe what the opening asks, what the middle adds and what the ending answers.
Inspect whether footage, documents and coded explanation follow the same identified example,
and whether each transition supplies new understanding at a comprehensible pace. Compare your
first reconstruction with the director's rationale; a plausible rationale can't clear a
missing picture. Keep these findings inside the current comprehension and continuity fields.
No new score, medium quota or presenter requirement is introduced.

Record those observations in the existing comprehension, continuity and defect fields. A moving
prop can be source-related yet fail to explain the sentence. Do not classify an absent principal
action or failed comprehension as merely style at the creative cap. Preserve actual scores and
rejections; the worksheet and dossier are guidance, not new approval evidence or scoring weights.

From October 3rd, 2026, read any completion_readings bound in your current packet. Capacity recovery preserves every actual verdict, fixed rubric and source or technical gate. Reconstruct the film before director rationale. A grant is never film approval.

For current directed-film-v2 films, load the bound complete MODERN_FILM.md and STORY_ART.md.
Return timed exact-film modern_observations for first_frame, visual_progression, shot_variety,
performed_turn, pace, closing_answer and finished_art, each with pass, start_s, end_s and
observed. Watch at normal speed before reading the director rationale. New generated images
must be relevant, visibly finished and used in performed tasks; a static illustrated slideshow
still fails. Put each failed modern observation in defects and hard_fails under the fixed rubric.
Preserve actual score and failure. Current engagement and art finish cannot use artistic deferral.


## Narration and picture use one clock

For new production from October 8th, every spoken clause has a narration-picture-v1 binding in board.narration_picture. Write exact clause text, concrete subject_ids, executable action_id, source claim_ids, scene_id, cue_ids and event_ids before voice production. Cover all words and qualifiers once in their original order. The registered episode declares which views actually implement those subjects and actions. A topic match, caption or label cannot replace a pictured causal step.

Before voice exists, use timing_mode authored with an explicit provisional cue plan for the silent two-treatment comparison. These estimated windows approve only planning. After alignment, board_retime.py replaces them with measured_caption_boundaries from the actual captions and acoustic word stream. Timed capture, preship and delivery require those measured inputs and reject an authored clock.

After acoustic alignment, compile every clause window from complete measured caption boundaries and the matched positional word stream. Use modern_film.compile_narration with the actual captions and words. Derive cut handoffs from silence between clauses. Only framing subdivisions inside the same subject/action may use fractions. Renderer performances consume requireNarration on the film-global clock, and retain completed consequences across cuts. Never stretch speech, scale cue times, or proportionally place a different narrated action inside a scene.

Run scripts/modern_film.py with --board, --captions, --words, --script and --claims before timed capture and preship. The gate rejects missing or duplicated clauses, omitted qualifiers, stale timing, wrong condition identity, incompatible renderer views and gaps in matching picture coverage. These checks establish bindings, not audience understanding. Code, phone and final reviewers inspect the actual subject and performed action for every clause. Return narration_picture_observations bound to the exact film, with ordered clauses containing id, pass, exact start_s/end_s and observed. Preserve a wrong or absent picture as a source/comprehension blocker even if provider metadata says pass.

A current clause must remain understandable with its captions covered. Introduce the spoken subject before its clause begins, perform the narrated change while it is heard, and retain the relevant result through the clause end. Distinguish selection, analysis, test condition, observed result and clinical limit. Generic clinical forms, a repeated test picture under an AI-selection line, or the normal condition under a patient-variant line fail this contract.

# Autonomous completion capacity

Effective October 3rd, 2026. The owner prohibits ending an autonomous Dispatch run at an internal resource ceiling or host review capacity error. Done means an accepted shipped video, deployed permanent bytes, canonical phone playback and the verified correctly addressed unsent Gmail draft.

This standing instruction authorizes the mandatory completion capacity policy in config/autonomous_completion.json. Preserve each run's original frozen envelope and every cumulative charge. Record necessary completion increments as separate evidence-bound controller events. Never reset usage or treat a grant as picture, score or shipment approval.

Before a correction, consolidate exact independent failures, preserve the strongest complete cut and run production-budget with its repair plan. A failed minimum action or held-slide treatment has no finish-current route. Use the independent source-backed pivot and the controller completion-capacity command to fund the complete remaining code, silent phone, final timed phone, native hero, final audiovisual, scorer and delivery path before paid work. Reserve every attempt first.

The creative cap still ends optional polish. Mandatory minimum action, factual, source, rights, legibility, comprehension, audio, captions, runtime and release integrity failures require autonomous correction. A standing grant funds only this completion work. It does not authorize duplicate research, speculative rigs, extra treatment shopping or a new edition that hides an unfinished one.

For an actual unavailable host, preserve the observed transport error and follow prompts/phases/review-availability.md through the configured independent provider with the same role, guides and fixed rubric. A resource deficit is not a transport error. Keep all three final audiovisual lenses and three separate independent scorers.

After normal or bounded creative release authorization, stop creative editing and finish exact-head CI, merges, deployment, permanent byte verification, canonical phone playback and unsent draft readback. Retain real rejected verdicts and scores. Neither a preview, checkpoint, resource boundary nor a local publishable package ends production. Never send email or post socially.

This dated owner instruction overrides older text that made an internal exhausted envelope an approval stop. The original envelope remains an accounting baseline, and audited standing completion increments are its authorized exception.

## Current modern-film editions

From October 8th, initialization adopts config/autonomous_completion_v2.json. The earlier policy
and its exact retained bytes stay valid for historical ledgers. The current complete remaining
path includes necessary fresh ImageGen story art. An independent exact-film failed modern
engagement or finish observation admits modern-film-floor recovery. Retain original resource
allocation, failed cut, actual observations and cumulative charges. No capacity event approves
artwork or restores a legacy renderer. Optional polish stops; the mandatory current floor is
repaired through the existing source-backed completion path.
